# Loyalty Widget & Branding

## Classic widget vs Unified widget

Joy launched the **Unified widget** as a complete rebuild of the storefront loyalty UI.

| | Classic widget | Unified widget |
|---|---|---|
| **Who has it** | Merchants who installed Joy before the Unified launch | Merchants who installed Joy after the Unified widget launch |
| **Status badge** | "Classic is live" | "Unified widget — Live" |
| **Focus** | Points and rewards only | All-in-one: profile, orders, wishlist, recommendations, points, rewards, and more |
| **Design editor** | 4 horizontal tabs (Widget theme / Membership card / Display / Advanced) | Full sidebar editor with live storefront preview |
| **Customization** | Limited color/font options | Every color, font, spacing, border radius exposed as CSS properties — full brand control |
| **Performance** | Standard | Lazy-loaded, smaller bundle on first paint |
| **Data** | — | Same Joy data — programs, points, customers carry over untouched |

## How to check which widget you're on

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design** section — it shows two cards, **Unified widget** and **Classic widget**:
- Badge says **"Classic is live"** → you're on Classic
- Badge says **"Unified is live"** on the Unified card → you're on Unified

## Switching from Classic to Unified

Merchants on Classic can switch at any time:
- **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Switch to Unified** button (at the Widget design section heading)
- All existing Joy data (points, programs, customers) carries over — nothing is lost
- Both versions never run simultaneously

## Free setup offer

When a merchant asks about the difference or expresses interest in switching, offer the free setup service:

> "We're offering a free setup service where our team styles your unified loyalty widget or loyalty page to match your store's branding, colors, layout — the whole thing. You won't need to lift a finger. We'll take care of it and send you the result to review. Do you want to give it a try?"

If merchant accepts → collect store URL and escalate to team with `<escalate_human>`.

## Classic widget — features still on Classic only

Milestone program UI, interactive website popup, Wallet pass / QR, Submit receipt program, branded reminder popup — these auto-fallback to Classic UI even on Unified stores.

---

## How to identify Widget v4

The easiest tell: go to **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Setup**. 
- **V4**: opens a full **Widget design editor** with a left sidebar (Settings / Header / Body / Footer / Extensions / Advanced) and a live storefront preview on the right.
- **V3**: opens a page with 4 horizontal tabs (Widget theme / Membership card / Display / Advanced settings).

## Widget design editor — path

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**

## Sidebar structure

### Settings
- **Design** — Preset Theme (Midnight, Forest, Ocean, Warm, Blush, Minimal, Dark, Slate) + Industry inspiration presets (Fashion, Beauty & Wellness, Food & Drink, Home & Garden, Sports & Fitness, Pets & Animals, Men's Grooming, Default), **Style preset** (Default / Neo-Brutalism — a separate "shape language" axis from color, see "Style preset — Neo-Brutalism" below), Primary color, Background color, Layout (Widget / Drawer), Position on desktop, Earn & Redeem layout (Tabs / Separate blocks), Text size, Border radius (None / Sharp / Soft / Rounded / Extra), Currency icon (None / Emoji / Image), Fonts (Heading + Body), Text theme colors, Buttons (color, text color, text case), Cards (heading/body text color, background, border). Also has an **On-brand** design scan to auto-detect colors/logo/imagery from the storefront — see "On-brand design scan" below (do not confuse with the text-only On-brand button under Content & Translations).
- **Launcher** — Float button style (Icon only / Label only / Icon & label / Point balance), Point balance label, Label section color, Button size (S/M/L/XL), Border radius (Pill/Rounded/Square), Alignment (Bottom left / Bottom right)
- **Content & Translations** — inline editor to customize all widget text labels (Program name, Launcher, Guest view, Logged in, Points display, Tier perks, Program tabs, Section titles, Coupons, Referral, Redeem flow, Earn flow, bundle chip templates like `Save {{value}} · {{type}}`, etc.). Buttons: **Revert to default** (reset all text) and **On-brand** (AI-rewrite labels to match store voice — text only; for auto-detecting colors/logo/imagery see "On-brand design scan" below).

### Header
- **Header** — Program name text size (Small/Medium/Large), Header background color (or "Use primary"), Header text color, Logo (Add image, or paste image URL, or "Use store logo" button — any aspect ratio, height configurable), Header background image (upload; recommended **8:5 ratio, 800×500px, under 200KB**) + overlay opacity slider

### Body
Each block can be **toggled on/off** and **drag-and-drop reordered**. Click any block to edit its content, text, or images inline.

| Block | Notes |
|---|---|
| Membership card | Card layout (Compact/Classic), Default avatar, Guest card image, Member card image, Sign-in settings, Open widget after login |
| My coupons | Optional **Show QR code** button per available coupon (off by default) — see "Coupon QR code" below |
| Refer a friend | Shows the customer's own referral activity — who they referred and each referral's status — plus summary counts (e.g. referred / completed), inline in the block |
| Ways to earn | — |
| Ways to redeem | — |
| Recently viewed | Off by default |
| Recommended | Off by default |
| Recent activity | Off by default |
| Milestones | Shows a claimable-count badge when a step is unlocked and unclaimed (Customer's Choice rewards) — see kb_milestone |
| My QR code | — |
| Wallet pass | — |
| Subscription portal | Requires Joy Subscription extension |
| Wishlist | Off by default; works with **Joy Wishlist**, and also auto-detects **Swym Wishlist Plus** or **Wishlist King** if the store has one of those installed instead — no extra config needed to switch provider |

**Membership card custom blocks** — click the `+` under Membership card to add: Heading, Rich text, Button, Divider, Image banner, Image with text, Custom link, Custom CTA.

### Footer
- **Footer menu** — bottom navigation tabs. Drag to reorder, toggle visibility, customize each tab.
  - **Display mode**: Icons & labels / Icons only / Labels only
  - **Active indicator style**: Pill / (others)
  - Tabs: **Home, Rewards, Orders, Wishlist, Reviews, Profile** (each toggleable; Wishlist/Reviews hidden by default)
- **Profile** (the Profile tab's sub-pages, each toggleable): Account info, Referral link, Social accounts, Shipping addresses, Settings, Log out, Reviews. The **Settings** sub-page includes SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent — see "SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent in Profile" below.

## SMS/WhatsApp marketing consent in Profile

The Unified widget's **Profile → Settings** sub-page lets customers opt in to SMS/WhatsApp marketing directly from the widget, without leaving the storefront.

- **Where:** Widget → **Profile → Settings**.
- **Flow:** the customer enters their phone number and toggles consent to receive SMS/WhatsApp messages. If the customer has no phone number on file yet, they first see an **"Add your phone"** prompt in Account info — once a number is saved, the consent toggle becomes available. The phone number field **auto-detects and prefills the country code** based on the customer's storefront locale/market, so most customers don't have to look up or type their own dialing prefix — they can still change it if it's wrong.
- **What Joy does:** Joy writes the consent to the customer's record on **Shopify**, so the merchant can use it for marketing/automation (e.g. segments, flows).
- **What Joy does NOT do:** Joy does not send the SMS/WhatsApp messages itself — actual sending still goes through whatever SMS/WhatsApp platform the merchant already has connected. Joy's role here is only to capture and store the consent.

**Related earning program:** opting in to SMS marketing consent from this same Profile → Settings toggle can also earn the customer points, if the merchant has set up the **Subscribe SMS marketing** earning program — see kb_earning-programs.

### Extensions
Toggle on/off: **Wishlist**, **Bundling**, **Reviews**, **Subscription**, **Survey**. Each extension that needs a companion app (e.g. Wishlist) shows an "Install app / Watch setup guide / Verify installation" panel and a layout/options block (e.g. Wishlist layout: Carousel / Grid / List, image hover effect). The Wishlist extension auto-detects **Joy Wishlist**, **Swym Wishlist Plus**, or **Wishlist King** — whichever wishlist app the store has installed — with no extra config needed to pick the provider.

### Advanced
- **Display** — hide widget from guests, page restriction, instant popup, hide widget button
- **Popup** — popup behavior settings
- **Custom links** — redirect links for earning programs
- **Custom CSS** — custom CSS field for pixel-level overrides
- **External discounts** — off by default; shows up to 10 external (non-Joy) discount codes inside the widget's My Coupons block. See "Show External Discounts in My Coupons" below.

## Show External Discounts in My Coupons

Joy can surface discount codes that were **not created by Joy** — e.g. codes made directly in Shopify, or by another app like Klaviyo — inside the widget's **My Coupons** section, next to the customer's regular Joy coupons. This solves the case where a merchant wants a non-Joy discount to be visible to customers in the loyalty widget.

- **Where to enable:** Widget design editor → **Advanced → External discounts**.
- **Default:** off.
- **Limit:** the merchant selects up to **10** discount codes to show.
- **Eligibility:** Joy only displays a selected code to customers who actually qualify for it (matching the discount's own audience — All customers / Specific customers / Segment — and whether it's still within its active dates and usage limit). Each visible code shows its value and conditions.
- This is a Unified widget feature; it lives in the same Advanced tab as Display/Popup/Custom CSS settings.

## Coupon QR code (My Coupons)

Opt-in, **off by default**. Adds a **Show QR code** button next to **Apply coupon now** on each available coupon in the **My Coupons** block. Tapping it renders a QR code that encodes Shopify's shareable discount link (`https://<shop>.myshopify.com/discount/<code>`):

- **Phone camera** — scanning it opens the storefront with the discount applied to the cart.
- **Shopify POS** — scanning it with the POS camera or a 2D barcode scanner applies the discount directly to the POS cart, the same way Shopify's own shareable discount QR works.

**Enable at:** Widget V4 editor → Sections → **My coupons** → **Show QR code for coupons**.

- Works for both Joy reward coupons and external (non-Joy) Shopify discounts shown in My Coupons — one setting covers both.
- **Not shown** for gift cards, coupons with an empty code, or coupons that are used/expired/revoked.
- **This is convenience, not fraud protection.** For external Shopify discounts the code is shop-wide/shared, so a QR of it doesn't prove who's holding it — Joy-issued reward coupons are already per-customer, so the QR doesn't change their security posture either way.

## On-brand design scan (Widget V4 — auto-detect colors, logo, imagery)

Distinct from the **On-brand** button under **Content & Translations** (which AI-rewrites the widget's text labels) — this is a separate **design** scan that reads the merchant's actual storefront and auto-fills the widget's colors, logo, and imagery to match their brand, in one click.

**Where:** Widget V4 editor → **Settings → Design → On-brand**. The merchant provides their storefront URL; Joy loads it and detects: the primary/accent color (from the add-to-cart button), background color, a secondary brand color, text and heading color, the store logo, an avatar image, and hero/banner imagery.

- **Nothing is applied silently** — every detected color is shown in the panel and is editable before the merchant applies it.
- Reads modern CSS color formats too (`oklch()`, `hsl()`, `hwb()`, `lab()`, etc.), not just hex/rgb, so it works on storefronts built with newer CSS.
- If a detected text/background color pair would fail accessibility contrast, Joy skips that pair rather than applying an unreadable combination.

If a merchant reports the scan picked an odd or clearly wrong color (e.g. pulled from a cart-drawer heading, or came out fully transparent), this is a known class of edge case — collect the storefront URL and escalate if a retry doesn't produce a usable result.

## Style preset — Neo-Brutalism (Widget V4, beta)

A second visual language for the widget, independent from the color palette. **Style** (`Default` or `Neo-Brutalism`) controls the **shape language** — borders, shadows, corner radius, type weight — while the **palette** controls colors only; changing one doesn't change the other's setting, but switching style does reset the palette (see below).

- **Where:** Widget V4 editor → **Settings → Design → Style preset**. Switching styles asks for confirmation first, because it overwrites the current color palette — Neo-Brutalism seeds one of its own 8 color palettes so the widget looks coherent immediately, rather than sharp corners paired with the merchant's old colors.
- **Switching back to Default** restores the previous shape/corner-radius settings but **keeps whatever colors were active** — a style toggle is not meant to destroy the merchant's color customization in either direction.
- **Currently marked Beta** in the picker (a visible badge next to the option, not just a note elsewhere in the panel). Known gaps at launch: the neo look isn't fully applied to every widget surface yet (e.g. coupon and balance-history cards, footer nav still look like Default), and a few of the built-in Neo-Brutalism color palettes fail accessibility contrast on their header text. Set expectations with merchants as an **opt-in beta look**, not a finished, uniformly-applied theme — the flag will come off once these gaps are closed.

## Widget V4 — simpler default style, configurable back button, editor Inspect mode, mobile swipe

All of the below are Widget V4 only, set at **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**.

- **Default style preset is simpler now.** The `Default` style preset (Settings → Design → Style preset) now renders with cleaner surfaces and single-colour accents — this changed for merchants who haven't customized their style yet, it does **not** overwrite a merchant's already-saved custom colors/spacing. A merchant who set up their widget a while ago and now sees a different look on a fresh/reset widget should be told this is the new default look, not a bug.
- **Back button is now configurable.** Sub-pages inside the widget (e.g. drilling into a program or a Milestones step) can show a back button, controlled from the widget design editor rather than always-on or always-off.
- **Inspect mode in the editor.** In the live storefront preview (right pane of the Widget V4 editor), turning on **Inspect** and clicking any element on the preview jumps the editor straight to the block/section controlling that element — useful when a merchant isn't sure which sidebar section controls something they see on the storefront.
- **Swipe navigation on mobile.** Customers on mobile can swipe left/right to move between pages inside the widget, in addition to tapping footer menu tabs or the back button.

## Open the widget from the theme's account button (Widget V4)

Widget V4 can be opened from the storefront theme's own **account icon/button** (the header account/login link most themes already have), instead of only the floating Joy launcher.

**Location:** Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget design → **Display** → toggle **"Open Joy from the theme account button or link."**

**How it works:** turning this on rewrites the theme's account/login link to open the Joy widget (internally it repoints the link to `#joy-open`) — no custom code needed from the merchant.

**To keep one specific account/login link native** (not hijacked to open Joy — e.g. a link that should still go to Shopify's native customer account page), add the attribute `data-joy-account-ignore` to that element.

**Widget mode** (separate setting, same area) controls what content the widget shows once opened:
- **Loyalty** — shows points/rewards content.
- **Customer Accounts** — shows orders, addresses, profile, and product discovery instead; hides loyalty content. Meant for merchants who haven't launched their loyalty program yet, so the widget still works as an account hub (similar to a Klaviyo Hub).

## Live preview controls

The editor's right pane is a live storefront preview with an **"Embed active"** status badge. The "Preview as" toolbar lets the merchant simulate different viewers without affecting the live store:
- **Device** — Desktop / Mobile
- **Customer** — Signed in / Guest
- **VIP tier** — Member (no VIP) / Simulate VIP active
- **Customise customer data…** — set sample points/tier for the preview
- **View on store** — open the real storefront in a new tab

## How to change/replace images

A preset theme (or industry inspiration) only sets **sample images** — it never locks them. To use your own images, you edit each image where it lives, block by block; there is no single "images" page.

**Steps:**
1. Open **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**.
2. In the left sidebar, navigate to Sections ⛶,  click the **Header** or the **Body block** that contains the image you want to change (e.g. Header logo, Header background image, Membership card → Default avatar / Guest card / Member card image, or an Image banner / Image with text custom block) (https://capture.avada.io/i/3MlO1vlvJ8z3).
3. In the editor (middle pane), find that image's field and click **Upload image** (or paste an image URL) to replace it. The live preview on the right updates immediately.
4. **Save.**

**Where images live:**

| Image | Where to change it |
|---|---|
| Program logo | Header → Logo (Add image / paste URL / Use store logo) |

> **"Your Logo" placeholder showing instead of the store's logo:** this is expected, not a bug. When no image has been uploaded to the Header → Logo field, Joy displays a default **"Your Logo"** placeholder there. The fix is simply to upload a logo (or click **Use store logo**) at **Header → Logo** — no need to escalate.
| Header background | Header → Header background image (8:5, 800×500px, <200KB) |
| Default avatar (no uploaded avatar) | Body → Membership card → Default avatar (1:1, 200×200px, <200KB) |
| Guest card banner | Body → Membership card → Guest card |
| Member card banner | Body → Membership card → Member card image |
| Custom image block | Body → Membership card → `+` → Image banner / Image with text |

> Tip: the banner shown inside the membership card in the preview (e.g. the "Fuel your adventure" image) is a Membership card image block — click Membership card to swap it.
---

## Display & Popup settings (page restriction, hide widget) — all plans

All these settings are available on **every plan, including Starter (free)** — there is no plan restriction on them. Both live under **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup → Advanced**, but on two different sidebar tabs:

**Advanced → Display:**
- **Hide widget from guests** (also labeled **"Display after login"** in the Unified widget V4 editor — same toggle, turning it on means the widget only shows to logged-in/identified customers and stays hidden for guests/non-logged-in visitors) — only show the widget to logged-in customers.
- **Hide widget button** — turn off to always display the widget button.

**Advanced → Popup:**
- **Instant popup** — Off by default; enable to let the widget open automatically when customers visit the store.
- **Page restriction** ("Show on specific pages") — Off by default (widget shows on all pages). Toggle on, then check the pages to show on: Home page, Product pages, Collection pages, Cart pages, Blog pages, Custom page.

> Common mistake: "Show on specific pages" is **not** under Display — it's under **Popup**, alongside Instant popup.

## Brand colors

Joy auto-detects your store's primary, secondary, accent palette. Edit at **Joy Admin → Settings → Colors**. These appear in color pickers throughout Joy.

## Display types

- **Floating widget** — small chatbox-style button (default)
- **Drawer** — large side panel similar to cart drawer
- Mobile slides up from bottom for both

## Setup path

**Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup** — controls layout, color, position, advanced custom CSS.

## Safe preview

Duplicate your theme in Shopify, enable the Joy app embed on the duplicate, and use Shopify's Preview to test without affecting live customers.

## Enable on storefront

**Theme Editor → App Embeds → Joy Loyalty - Widget → Save**.

---

| Method | New customer accounts | Shopify Plus + Legacy | Setup |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sign in with Shop App | ✅ | ✅ | Toggle only |
| Email OTP | ❌ | ✅ | Paste Multipass key |
| Sign in with Google | ❌ | ✅ | Toggle only |
| Sign in with Facebook | ❌ | ✅ | Toggle only |

If your store uses **new customer accounts**, only Shop App login appears. Email OTP, Google, Facebook need Shopify Plus + legacy accounts and use Multipass.

## Setup

**Joy Admin → Settings → Additional Features → toggle Sign in with Shop App** (or other methods).

---

All in **Joy Admin → On-site content → Widget → Widget design → Setup**.

## Referral popup

Customizable popups: **Referral Popup** (invite), **Referral Rewards Popup** (reward messaging), **Referral Success Popup**. Choose template or custom; configure content, position, frequency. If you skip the dedicated referral floating button, customers still access referral via the main widget.

## Visit website popup

Strategic on-arrival nudge. Configure two states: **Before Sign-In** and **After Sign-In**. Customize button icon, position (e.g., bottom-right).

## Reward reminder

Auto pop-ups when customer has unused/qualifying rewards.

**Path:** Joy Admin → On-site content → **Popups** → Reward reminder → Setup. (The Popups tab is a top-level tab of On-site content — there is **no** "Branding" step. The reward reminder is a legacy block being deprecated; on Unified/V4 shops it's folded into the widget and the Popups tab only shows while the shop still has these blocks.)

| Reminder | Trigger |
|---|---|
| Birthday reward | Birthday approaching/today |
| Milestone achieved | Reached a new milestone |
| Unused discount | Has unredeemed coupon |
| Reward redemption | Has enough points |
| Visit website | Visits the store |

The Reward reminder Setup screen only configures **when/how the reminder pops up** (trigger, display mode, text). It does **NOT** have an image-upload field.

> **Changing the images shown in a reward reminder / membership card popup:** those images are NOT edited in the Popups tab. They are Membership card images inside the widget editor. Route the merchant to **On-site content → Widget → Widget design → open the editor → Sections → Membership card → Guest card image / Member card image → Upload image** (see "How to change/replace images" above). This is the correct fix when a merchant says the reward/reminder popup "still shows the stock/sample image."

## Display modes

- **Show highest priority only** (default) — drag to reorder priority list
- **Show all sequentially** — one after another, each dismissed per session

# Referral Program

Set up at **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Referrals**. Basic features on All plans; advanced (Shopify customer/order tagging) on Essential, Advanced, Ultimate.

## Reward types

| For | Available reward types |
|---|---|
| **Referee** (new customer) | Points, Store credit, Discount %, Discount amount |
| **Referrer** | Points, **Points (based on order value)**, Store credit (fixed), Store credit (% of referee order), Discount %, Discount amount |

**Points based on order value (added 2026-08-10):** set at **Reward method → Points based on order value**. Merchant enters a points-per-$1 rate applied to the referee's order **subtotal after discount** (shipping and tax excluded) and chooses a rounding rule; a preview shows an example calculation. This exists so a merchant running a points-based loyalty program can reward referrers proportionally without granting Store Credit permissions they may not want to give.

- **Tier-based rewards** — Customize referrer reward by VIP tier. For the points-based-on-order-value method, turning this on switches the setup screen from a single preview number to a reminder to set a rate for each tier individually.
- **Max amount cap on % discount** — e.g., "15% off, up to $30" — set independently per side, off by default
- The configured rate shows to customers on the Referral block of **Widget V4**, e.g. *"2 points per $1 your friend spends."*

## Referral claim popup V3 — new installs / opt-in only, not all shops

**Not every shop is on this yet — there is no automatic backfill.** V3 is only turned on for new installs and for existing shops that switch it on via an internal DevZone toggle. If a merchant describes a referral popup that doesn't match what's below (e.g. a single success card with just a code and no email-capture step), they're on the older popup version — troubleshoot against that instead of this section.

- **What's different:** the page a referred friend lands on after clicking the referral link is now a two-step **claim → reveal** flow — the friend enters their email to claim, then the reward code is revealed — instead of the older one-step success card. The popup also pulls its colors/fonts from the merchant's Widget V4 design, so a merchant who styled their widget gets a matching popup automatically.
- **Editor:** merchants get a dedicated popup editor (Content / Blocks / Design / Translations tabs) to customize copy, layout/template, and which blocks show (headline, sub-copy, email capture, CTA, terms, code reveal, countdown, "shop now", etc.).
- **The old referrer-side "invite" popup is retired on V3** — one popup/editor now covers both the referrer's invite experience and the referee's claim experience; there's no separate invite-popup toggle to look for on a V3 shop.
- **Guest-friendly coupons:** a referred friend who isn't a customer account yet can still see and use their claimed coupon — the code is remembered in their browser (not tied to an account) for 90 days, so closing the popup doesn't lose it. It shows up in the widget's My coupons, or a coupons-only view on the account/loyalty page for guests.

## Referral redirection URL

Default = homepage. Change to any landing page (e.g., a campaign page).

## Sharing channels

Customers share their unique link via the loyalty widget across selected social/email channels. Email invite (see next chunk) is built-in.

---

## Flow

1. Referrer shares their unique link
2. Referee clicks link → lands on referral page → enters email to claim → **7-day cookie** stored on device → activity = pending. The **referee's** reward (coupon / store credit) is issued at this claim step; the **referrer's** reward stays pending until the referee actually orders.
3. Referee places order with the **same email** → activity = complete on thank-you page → both rewarded.

**When the referrer's reward is granted** — the referrer is rewarded only after the referee places a qualifying order, following the shop's earn-status setting (same as points earning):

- **Reward on Paid** (default, `earnByOrderStatus = financial_status`): granted as soon as the referee's order is **Paid**.
- **Reward on Fulfilled / Partial**: the reward waits until the order reaches that fulfilment status. While the order is Paid but not yet fulfilled, the referral shows **"Awaiting fulfilment"** (this is normal — it means the order was placed and is waiting to fulfil, not that something failed).

## Troubleshooting (referrer didn't get reward)

- **Different emails** — referee used different email at claim vs checkout. Both sides need same email
- **App pixel disabled** — check **Shopify Admin → Settings → Customer Events → Joy** is enabled. Toggle program off/on to re-sync
- Cookie expired (>7 days between click and purchase)

## Common false negatives when testing

- **"Running in test mode" message** means the referral program is in **Sandbox / preview** — go live for real rewards to be issued.
- **Same PC / same browser:** on a device where the merchant is logged into their own store, the referral page may show only the code without prompting for a friend's email. Test in incognito, another account, or a phone to see the real behaviour.

## Anti-cheat

Built-in fraud prevention stops customers gaming the program with multiple accounts. Configure limits per program in the referral settings. When anti-cheat is enabled, a referral is blocked when the referrer and referee share the **same browser, same email, or same IP address**, or reuse the **same order**. The referee's order must also have a **subtotal greater than $0** — a $0 order does not qualify the referrer for a reward.

## Referral limits

- **Referral limit per customer** (field label in **Joy Admin → Reward programs → Referrals → referral settings**) — caps the number of successful referrals a single referrer can earn from. Example: set to 5 to let each member earn rewards from a maximum of 5 successful referrals; combine with a fixed per-referral reward (e.g. store credit or points equivalent to a fixed amount) to naturally cap the total a member can earn.
- **Plan-based limit** — the **Free plan** caps how many referral orders can be rewarded. To lift the cap, the merchant upgrades to a paid plan. Higher plans raise or remove this limit.

## Reward revocation on refund

If the referee's qualifying order is **fully refunded**, the referrer's reward is **automatically revoked** when the merchant has enabled **Auto-revoke referrer reward** on the referral program (points are deducted back and a revoke activity is logged). If the setting is off, the referrer keeps the reward even after a refund.

Available on **All plans**. Referrer enters friend's email in the widget → system auto-sends a branded invitation email containing the referrer's name, the discount/reward, and the referral link.

Delivery channels supported:
- Joy's built-in email
- Klaviyo
- Shopify Flow

The invite email goes to the **referee** (carrying the referrer's unique link), not to the referrer. Settings live at **Joy Admin → Settings → Notifications** for the built-in template; for automation, configure at **Referral program → Referral flow → Automated email sharing**. To build this in **Klaviyo**, choose the Klaviyo trigger **"Joy: Referral Link Sent"** and build the flow around it.

**Prefix gotcha:** `Joy: ` is the default event-name prefix. Shops that connected **Klaviyo between 2025-10-08 and 2026-03-05** were backfilled with prefix `Klaviyo Joy: ` instead — for those shops the trigger is named `Klaviyo Joy: Referral Link Sent`, not `Joy: Referral Link Sent`. The Joy Admin UI always previews the `Joy: ` form regardless of which prefix a shop actually has, so if the trigger isn't firing, check when Klaviyo was connected and have the merchant look for both name variants in Klaviyo's metric list (see kb_integrations-email).

Two related Klaviyo/Omnisend events for the rest of the referral flow: `Joy: Referral Friend Complete` (fires when the referred friend completes their first qualifying purchase) and `Joy: Referee Claim Reward` (fires when the friend claims their reward).

**`Joy: Referee Claim Reward` — event property names (confirmed working since the 2026-09-08 fix):** the `customer` on this event is already the **referee** (the one claiming), so the useful new field is `Referrer email` — the person who referred them. The event carries exactly three custom properties: `Referrer email`, `Reward type` (`coupon` or store-credit), and `Reward` (the actual coupon code for a coupon reward, or the store-credit amount for a store-credit reward — same field name, two possible content shapes depending on `Reward type`).

**Before 2026-09-08, real sends of this event carried NONE of these properties** — only the "Send test" preview in Klaviyo's trigger picker (Admin → Integration → Klaviyo → step 3) had fixture values, which is why the test preview looked right while real events differed. If a merchant's Klaviyo flow references a coupon-code variable name that doesn't match `Reward` above, the flow was likely built against an older real event (pre-fix, no fields at all) or copied a guessed name from an earlier support reply — have them rebuild the flow's filter/personalization against `Referrer email` / `Reward type` / `Reward`.

When the friend purchases, both sides get rewards + confirmation emails.

## Merchant referral program (refer-a-merchant)

This is a **separate program from the customer referral program above** — here the merchant refers other Shopify merchants to Joy, not customers referring friends.

- **Set up:** No setup needed by the merchant. Eligible merchants see a banner "Referral Program" on the **Homepage** or **Settings → Subscription** page, and get a unique referral code/link to share with other Shopify merchants.
- **Eligibility:** Banner + program only shows to merchants who meet eligibility requirements (see Joy's merchant referral program guide for the current criteria).
- **Reward (referrer merchant) — Joy credit toward their next billing cycle**, tiered by the referrer's plan: **$29** on Essential, **$90** on Advanced, **$250** on Ultimate, per successful referral.
- **Reward (referred merchant):** discount off their first 3 months — 50% on Essential, 30% on Advanced, 20% on Ultimate.
- **Milestone bonus** (Advanced + Ultimate referrers only): extra **+$30** at 2 referrals, **+$100** at 5 referrals, **+$300** at 10 referrals.
- **Why it exists:** Joy's paid-ads/CAC channel for acquiring merchants was costly and underperforming, so merchant-to-merchant referral was added as a cheaper acquisition channel (added 2026-05-25).

## Referral export — Status detail column

Merchants export referral activity from the **Customers → Activities** export modal (same export used for points activity — see kb_analytics), ticking the columns they want, including **Status** and **Completed At**.

- **Status** keeps emitting the **raw** internal value — `pending_referral`, `complete_referral`, etc. — unchanged, so merchant scripts and spreadsheet formulas that already key off it keep working.
- A new, additive **Status detail** column carries the human-readable state instead: **Pending**, **Awaiting fulfillment**, **Completed**, or **Cancel**. It's included automatically whenever the merchant ticks the **Status** checkbox — there's no separate checkbox to turn it on, and it's emitted right after the Status column.
- **Completed At** is populated **only** for rows where the referral has actually completed (`Status` = Completed) — it's left blank for Pending, Awaiting fulfillment, and Cancel rows, since those haven't completed yet. If a merchant previously saw a filled-in Completed At on a non-completed row, that was the old (incorrect) behavior; it now correctly reflects only real completions.
